IDEA: VaultPay AI — an AI escrow agent for digital deliverables. A client's money
is authorized (held, not captured) before the work is inspected; an AI audits the
uploaded deliverable; on approval PayPal captures and the sealed files unlock, and
the freelancer is paid. On rejection the authorization is voided and nothing is
captured.

FRONTEND STRUCTURE:

Landing `/` — seven sections, in this order:
1. Problem — you paid, the work was broken, the money is gone. Real sentences.
2. Freeze — money is HELD not captured; amount in tabular monospace.
3. Vault — the manifest: file paths, sizes, hashes, each marked SEALED.
4. Interrogation — client asks a plain question, evidence stream answers.
5. Verdict — COMPUTED vs JUDGED shown as two clearly different things; include one
   real WARN/FAIL (`⚠ 1 test skipped — refund path, not in brief`) next to the passes.
6. Handshake — capture fires, webhook lands, files unlock; mono, with a transaction id.
7. Payoff + CTA — one memorable moment, then "Put it to the test" → overlay with three
   paths: SOLO (dominant: 60s, preloaded vault, replayed sandbox txn labelled with its
   real id and timestamp, no signup), WITH A FRIEND (two links + QR), LIVE SANDBOX
   (small de-emphasised link). Never force a PayPal login to reach the demo.

App — five routes, entered from the CTA via shared-element continuity, not a reload:
`/vault/new` — create: zip drop zone, amount, brief, optional staging URL, live
manifest preview resolving paths and sizes, "Seal vault" (disabled state explains
itself).
`/vault/[id]` — freelancer status: one dominant state token SEALED → AUDITING → PAID;
that flip is the loudest thing on screen; share link + QR; payout row appends on webhook.
`/v/[token]` — client portal, read-only: manifest with every row sealed and
non-clickable (no download affordance), beside an interrogation panel (fixed input,
evidence stream of provenance blocks), sticky footer with the HELD amount and
"Approve & Pay" disabled with an inline reason until the first result returns.
`/v/[token]/files` — released: same layout, tokens become RELEASED, rows get download
affordances, the payoff transition runs once and never again.
`/console` — audit ledger: dense, grouped by vault, filterable, live-updating on
webhook; columns separate COMPUTED from JUDGED and include source + latency; empty,
sorted and filtered states designed, not default.
`/demo` — a seeded state of the real app, never a separate mock.

Shared components, imported by both landing and app (never duplicated): manifest row,
state token, verdict chip, provenance block, freeze bar, amount readout.
Money states: SEALED, AUDITING, HELD, CAPTURED, VOIDED, RELEASED, PAID — one token
each, identical everywhere.

Research, choose, plan, then build the full frontend. No questions, no approval gates.

1. RESEARCH — use the ui-ux-pro-max skill (run its search script across style, color,
   typography, landing and ux domains, several different framings of my idea) and
   https://en970.github.io/ui-vault/ . UI Vault is client-rendered, so a plain fetch
   returns an empty shell — render it in a browser, or read its underlying data file /
   repo. Collect 8–12 named sources: for each, the mechanic you'll take and the one you
   won't. Record every search and every failed source honestly.

2. CHOOSE — pick one direction yourself. Compare 3 candidates on distinctiveness,
   fit to the idea, demo robustness and build cost. State the winner in one sentence,
   plus what you rejected from both sources and why.

3. PLAN — write PLAN.md before touching code: colour roles with hexes and reasons,
   type pairing, spacing rhythm, radius/border logic, every component with all its
   states (default, hover, focus, disabled, loading, error, empty), the motion spec
   (trigger → property → duration → easing → reduced-motion fallback), responsive
   breakpoints, and the file tree.

4. BUILD — one file per write, under ~200 lines. Tokens in one file, nothing hardcoded.
   Vertical slice first: one route, real data, real states, ugly is fine. Verify with a
   type check and build after every few files and report the actual output. Ask me
   nothing until it runs.

Rules: two transition types per page max; honour prefers-reduced-motion fully; body
text contrast ≥4.5:1; visible focus rings; no hover-only interaction; SVG icons, no
emoji; no default shadcn/dark-purple-gradient/cyberpunk-terminal looks. Never invent a
command, flag or source — if unsure, write "verify" and move on.

### Patterns worth borrowing

1. **Separate a preview from a sandbox.** A landing-page illustration (PostHog, Stripe) is cheap to enter; a sandbox (Stripe test mode, Resend test email) proves behavior more deeply but often requires setup or an account.
2. **Label the fiction at the point of use.** PostHog’s “Illustrative demo” and “All findings are sample data” are clear. Stripe’s sandbox/test-card language is also explicit. If a tour uses generated records, label them in the interface; if the demo pages don’t disclose that, say so rather than assume.
3. **Make collaboration a share action, not a signup funnel.** FigJam offers a useful host-to-visitor pattern: link, name/alias, limited temporary permissions, and explicit feature boundaries. QR can make the link easy to join in a room; the reviewed Figma Jam Session listing supports QR/link/code, while the official Open Session docs establish account-free visitor editing.
4. **Treat “guest” carefully.** Linear’s guest role narrows access after invitation; it does not remove the authentication step. That differs materially from Excalidraw’s account-free canvas or FigJam’s logged-out visitors.
5. **Recorded demos still count as low-friction previews—but not as product access.** Wistia’s public tour requires no login, yet visitors cannot explore a seeded account or replay transactions.

export type ManifestItem = {
  path: string;

export async function sha256Hex(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<string> {
  const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", bytes as unknown as BufferSource);
  return [...new Uint8Array(digest)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
}

export async function hashBlob(file: File): Promise<ManifestItem> {
  const buf = new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer());
  return {
    path: file.webkitRelativePath || file.name,
    size: buf.byteLength,
    hash: await sha256Hex(buf),
  };
}

/* Read a .zip client-side: real paths, real byte sizes, real sha-256 per entry. */
export async function manifestFromZip(zipFile: File): Promise<ManifestItem[]> {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await zipFile.arrayBuffer());
  const entries = unzipSync(bytes);
  const items: ManifestItem[] = [];

    if (!data.byteLength) continue;
    items.push({ path, size: data.byteLength, hash: await sha256Hex(data) });
  }
  items.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path));
  return items;
